one_liner: Single-threaded malloc built by stripping mimalloc's thread machinery; paper reports 1.03-1.05x over mimalloc and 1.17-1.19x over dlmalloc on SPEC CPU2017.
what_it_does: Exgen-Malloc is a research memory allocator (about 2,000 lines of C/C++) for programs that run on one thread. It is meant as a malloc/free replacement, but how it is linked or preloaded is not documented in what could be read, and no code release was found. It comes from the UT Austin group (Ruihao Li, Lizy K. John, Neeraja J. Yadwadkar) behind NextGen-Malloc and SpeedMalloc.
how_it_is_fast: It keeps mimalloc's segment/page layout (segments of about 4 MiB split into pages per size class) but uses one centralized heap instead of per-thread heaps, so there is no remote-free coordination. Each page has a single free-block list instead of mimalloc's sharded local/thread/remote free lists, and no atomics or synchronization are needed. The paper also tunes when memory is committed and when it is returned, trading allocation speed against footprint.
when_to_use: Single-threaded, allocation-heavy batch programs (SPEC CPU2017-style compilers, interpreters, simulators) where dlmalloc or glibc malloc is the current allocator
Single-threaded servers such as a redis-like event loop, where the paper reports a small gain (1.01x over mimalloc, 1.10x over dlmalloc)
Workloads shaped like mimalloc-bench's single-threaded tests, where the paper reports 1.93x over dlmalloc and 25.2% less memory than mimalloc
As a design reference for specializing mimalloc when you control the threading model
when_not_to_use: Any program that allocates or frees from more than one thread: the design removes the logic needed for thread safety and remote frees
Production use today: no public repository, license or release was found
If you already run mimalloc: the reported gain is only about 1.03-1.05x on SPEC and 1.01x on redis, inside the noise of many deployments
When you need hardening, profiling hooks or the mature tooling of jemalloc/mimalloc

integration.platforms: evaluated on two Intel Xeon platforms (per search snippet); others not documented
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — meant to replace malloc/free in single-threaded programs, but no artifact is available to drop in

gotchas: Search snippets disagree: one version says 1.17x over dlmalloc and 1.05x over mimalloc on SPEC CPU2017, another (the abstract wording the verifier used) says 1.19x and 1.03x; probably different arXiv/CAL revisions
A library that spawns a helper thread (logging, async I/O, OpenMP) quietly breaks the single-thread assumption
The 1.93x mimalloc-bench figure is against dlmalloc; against mimalloc the same suite shows only 1.02x
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose it over LWMalloc or rlsf only for study, since none of them ships a usable Exgen-Malloc; for a real single-threaded deployment, mimalloc (its parent) gets nearly the same speed with thread safety. SpeedMalloc from the same group targets multi-threaded code and needs new hardware.
verified_claims_summary: IEEE Computer Architecture Letters 2025 (arXiv 2510.10219) reports geometric-mean speedups on SPEC CPU2017 of 1.17-1.19x over dlmalloc and 1.03-1.05x over mimalloc, 1.10x/1.01x on redis-benchmark and 1.93x/1.02x on mimalloc-bench, with 6.2%/0.1%/25.2% memory savings over mimalloc, measured on two Intel Xeon machines; compiler, flags and exact CPU models are not known because every copy of the paper was blocked here and the numbers come from search snippets.
status_note: Research prototype with no public code or license found; reference-only, and the paper itself could not be opened in this session.
